senses.gloss: f.accustomed. Tanḥ. Noah 2 (מה של׳) מה שהיה ל׳ what each was used to eat (ed. Bub. ib. לָמוּד).

units: <cite ref="Niddah 22b:8">Nidd. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>כל ג״ש … אין ל׳ הימנה</he> from an analogy of textual words (v. <cite ref="C00581"><he>גְּזֵרָה</he></cite>) which are not free for interpretation (being necessary to the subject proper), you cannot derive any general rule; <cite ref="Niddah 22b:8">ib.</cite> <he>ל׳ ומשיבין</he> we may derive a rule, but it is open to argument; a. fr.—<he>הל׳ לפני חכמים</he> those who were permitted to argue before the scholars (e. g. Levi before Rabbi).
<cite ref="Meilah 9b">Meïl. 9ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 17b:4">Snh. 17ᵇ</cite> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 3).

<cite ref="Pesachim 25b:3">Pes. 25ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>הרי זה בא לְלַמֵּד ונמצא לָמֵד</he> (a proverbial phrase: behold this one comes as a teacher and turns out a learner) this is intended to throw light (on the case of a violated betrothed) and is at the same time receiving light.—Sifra introd. <he>דבר הל׳ מעניינו</he> something which is clearly understood from the context; a. fr.—

Y. Kidd. I, 59ᵃ עבריה למידה מבת חורין ועברי ל׳ מעבריה the case of the Ibriya (that a Hebrew handmaid can be acquired by a written deed) is learned from that of a free woman, and that of the Ibri (the Hebrew bondsman) from the Ibriya; נמצא לָ׳ מלָּ׳ consequently a case may be illustrated by one itself defined (only indirectly) by analogy; a. fr.
